label: prop:categorical-jet-prolongation
title: Jet object splitting and the failure of Hopf inheritance
html:
Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum universe with A commutative over a commutative ring R, let I = \ker(m \colon A \otimes A \to A), and let J^1(A) = (A \otimes A)/I^2 be the jet object. The section \ell \colon A \to J^1(A), a \mapsto [a \otimes 1], and the jet evaluation j^1 \colon J^1(A) \to A induced by m are algebra maps with j^1 \circ \ell = \mathrm{id}_A, so A is a direct summand of J^1(A) (jet object splitting). The jet object does not in general inherit the Frobenius–Hopf structure of A: over a field k of characteristic zero and for A = k[X] with X primitive, no multiplicative comultiplication on J^1(A) is compatible with both jet sections a \mapsto [a \otimes 1] and a \mapsto [1 \otimes a]. The prolongation object of the brane tower is therefore the tangent algebra T(A) = \mathrm{Sym}_A(\Omega^1_{A/R}), of which J^1(A) is the degree-\le 1 part (jet prolongation).
